Are edges with label '-' considered absent entirely, or can they be traversed as “null” edges that contribute no character to the string?
Is the graph guaranteed to have at most one edge between any ordered pair (i, j), and what should be done if the input contains contradictory information?
What is the required output format for the matrix: should numbers be separated by single spaces, and should there be a trailing space at the end of each line?

inline_prompts: We have a directed graph with N vertices, numbered 1, 2, \ldots, N. Information about the edges is given by N^2 characters C_{1, 1}, C_{1, 2}, \ldots, C_{1, N}, C_{2, 1}, \ldots, C_{N, N}. Here, each C_{i, j} is either a lowercase English letter or -. If C_{i, j} is a lowercase English letter, then there is exactly one directed edge from vertex i to vertex j labeled C_{i, j}. For each integer pair (i, j) with 1 \leq i, j \leq N, answer the following question: - Among all (not necessarily simple) paths from vertex i to vertex j whose concatenation of labels on the edges forms a palindrome, what is the length of the shortest such path? If there is no such path, the answer is -1. If i = j, is the empty path (length 0) considered valid? Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N C_{1, 1}C_{1, 2}\ldotsC_{1, N} C_{2, 1}C_{2, 2}\ldotsC_{2, N} \vdots C_{N, 1}C_{N, 2}\ldotsC_{N, N} Output Let A_{i, j} be the answer to the question for the pair (i, j). Print them in the following format: A_{1, 1} A_{1, 2} \ldots A_{1, N} A_{2, 1} A_{2, 2} \ldots A_{2, N} \vdots A_{N, 1} A_{N, 2} \ldots A_{N, N} Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 100 - N is an integer. - Each C_{i, j} is either a lowercase English letter or -.
